baer-heitev/1:_: And even if he sealed it. And even if he broke its pegs — see Taz:
beer-hagolah/1:ב: (ב) As Rashi explains there, and so Tur wrote.
beer-hagolah/1:ד: (ד) In chapter 3 of five [chapters of] Eruvin.
beer-hagolah/2:א: (א) There 93, and Shmuel's ruling was accepted by Tosafos.
beer-hagolah/2:ב: (ב) For if on Shabbat in a courtyard, even from courtyard to courtyard as well.
beer-hagolah/3:ב: (ב) Beit Yosef: if on Shabbat, since it was permitted it remains permitted, as above.
beer-hagolah/3:ו: (ו) For we say: we see as if the heads of the entryways of the walls of the small [courtyard] lean into the two length-walls of the large [courtyard].
beer-hagolah/4:ג: (ג) So it is in the mishnah and so brought in Tur.
beer-hagolah/4:ד: (ד) In the Gemara according to Rav.
beur-hagra/1:א: (א) Seif 1. And even if. Shabbat 101b; and likewise two ships, etc.; and Tosafos Eruvin 17a s.v. "joined an eruv."
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) And even if he sealed it. There 98b: they nullify and return, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And for Rambam. As with the ships mentioned — when they were severed they became forbidden from one to the other; they rejected this because there it is different since they are not fixed and they come to carry from one to the other via the sea which is karmelis; Rambam follows his view as he explained in commentary on the mishnah and in his composition there — even though enclosed they lack a partition, but they are explained like Rashi: adjacent.
beur-hagra/2:א: (ב) Seif 2. Even utensils of the house. Rashi there.
beur-hagra/2:ב: (ב) But a courtyard. Because they lack partitions, as written 17a.
beur-hagra/2:ג: (ג) A courtyard that was breached. Mishnah 94a.
beur-hagra/2:ד: (ד) To reshus ha-rabbim or. 95a, and Rav; see Tosafos s.v. "and Shmuel," etc.
beur-hagra/3:א: (ג) Seif 3. Before Shabbat. 93b: Rav said, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ב: (ב) And there is not in the breach. 9b: small, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ג: (ג) Utensils that remained. As above — Rashi there on the mishnah.
beur-hagra/3:ד: (ד) Unless they joined. 7b here, etc.; and Rashi there.
beur-hagra/3:ה: (ה) And this is, etc. And when walls. 34 — even one wall suffices.
beur-hagra/4:א: (ד) Seif 4. Before Shabbat. As above seif 3.
beur-hagra/4:ג: (ג) But if. Rashi there; and Tosafos there 89a s.v. "in partitions"; and Rosh there.
beur-hagra/4:ה: (ה) Four. For it is like holes of reshus ha-yachid — Shabbat 7b:
biur-halacha/1:א: And it was sealed on Shabbat — but if it was sealed while still day, even if it reopened on Shabbat they are forbidden, for they never acquired an eruv at all — acquisition of eruv is at bein hashemashot, and here there was no eruv at bein hashemashot since the opening was sealed; and even if they already joined for the Shabbat that passed for one Shabbat and that eruv still remains, they cannot rely on it this Shabbat after the opening opened, since it was already nullified while still day when it was sealed and does not revive at nightfall; and one who joins for a year — I join from the start for all Shabbatot and acquire the eruv on the first Shabbat when the opening was open — therefore even if afterward the opening was sealed and opened on another Shabbat, even at year's end the eruv returns and revives.
biur-halacha/1:ב: And even if he joined for a year, etc. — see Magen Avraham siman 383 where this law remains in doubt; however many later authorities resolve his difficulties there; nevertheless this law is not clear — behold the source of this law flows from Rosh beginning of Eruvin who brought proof from the law of ships that were severed and reconnected [Shabbat 101] that they return to their original permission, and Rosh proved it deals when they were severed on a weekday and nevertheless it helps when they reconnected afterward on Shabbat — for if severed on Shabbat, even if not reconnected they would be permitted because once permitted, permitted — and likewise in our matter; however per Tosafos [Shabbat 101] and likewise per many rishonim [Rambam see there, and in Rambam chapter 3, and Rashba and Ritva] who explained that baraita — even if severed on Shabbat it is forbidden because without the connection between them they drift from their place and it is like karmelis interrupting between them, and once permitted, permitted does not apply — thus there is no source for this law, for there it says they return to original permission because they were tied at the start of Shabbat and the eruv took effect — unlike our case where it was sealed at bein hashemashot and opened on Shabbat, and already Avkat Rochel raised this and likewise Magen Avraham in siman 1; however Tosafos' own view is not clear here, for in Eruvin 17 they wrote this law in the name of R' Yehuda and also proof from the ship — implying that for Tosafos' authors there were differing views, and Rosh ruled like Tosafos beginning of Eruvin [and what Magen Avraham wanted to reconcile Tosafos' views is unclear, for Rosh always follows Tosafos — and in Rosh it is explicit that his main proof is: if the baraita of ships deals with severance on Shabbat it would be permitted even without reconnecting, which is not Tosafos on that Shabbat — already raised in Nehar Shalom] — in any event this law is not clear per the rishonim above, and reasonably we should not say that what took effect on one Shabbat helps another Shabbat since at bein hashemashot of that Shabbat it was void; see siman 383 Beit Meir who also agrees with Magen Avraham that this law should be settled. Nevertheless after Rosh, Tur, Mechaber, and later authorities after Shulchan Aruch ruled this law, certainly we cannot reject it from practice; however regarding sealing intentionally that Magen Avraham brought from Maharil who permitted only when it opened before Shabbat, and likewise Avkat Rochel and Tosafos Yeshanim agreed — certainly we cannot be lenient here since from the root of the law even opening on Shabbat unintentionally is not clear to be lenient as above; and though some later authorities strain to reconcile Rama's view permitting in all cases, for practice it appears we should not be lenient as above; and in Netiv Chayim by Knesset Yisrael his view is that even Rama himself did not be lenient except when it opened afterward on a weekday.
biur-halacha/1:ג: And the opening was sealed on a weekday, etc. — and it appears the same when eruv chatzerot was nullified by another cause, e.g. the post in the alley was ruined and thereby the eruv of that alley was nullified — as explained end of siman 365: if the post was repaired on Shabbat by a gentile, etc., even though at bein hashemashot it was breached, nevertheless when repaired on Shabbat the eruv returns — since the eruv was made initially for the whole year; though one can distinguish somewhat that with breached partitions it is worse and joining for the year may not help — nevertheless in pressing circumstances one may be lenient here too, and I saw in one authority general 72 lenient here; however what he argues to be lenient even when joining for one Shabbat and it became known that on a weekday the post was ruined and repaired on Shabbat by a gentile — that courtyard eruv never took effect at all at bein hashemashot — because in that place they regularly make a post always, therefore it stands to be repaired, and when repaired later on Shabbat the courtyard eruv takes effect retroactively — his words are not clear at all; proof: for eruv via opening sealed on Shabbat Rashi explained e.g. a collapse fell against it — that certainly stands to be cleared, yet it is permitted only when sealed on Shabbat itself, because at bein hashemashot the eruv took effect and once permitted, permitted — not sealed while still day; therefore Shulchan Aruch was not lenient even when it stands to open except when joining for a year because the eruv already took effect on the first Shabbat, therefore it helps even if sealed afterward — not when joining for one Shabbat where the eruv never took effect at all at bein hashemashot; especially since the root law is not clear as above — therefore do not add to it; and what one authority wrote that some disagree in Tosafos reading "for both" — Or Zarua also wrote "for a year," and so in Rosh.
biur-halacha/2:א: And the wall was breached on Shabbat — meaning in its full [length] or more than ten amot.
biur-halacha/2:ב: To karmelis forbidden — see Beit Yosef who wrote this means forbidden to carry in the courtyard beyond four amot, but within four amot permitted even to carry from it to karmelis which is also like karmelis of water; Magen Avraham doubts this — perhaps the courtyard still lies upon it. Tosafos Shabbat 9 brought proof to permit, and so Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger and Nehar Shalom; in Avodat HaKodesh Sha'ar HaReshuyot din 1 it states explicitly forbidden, and so Tosafos there proved from Rashi 24 to forbid — see there; therefore it appears we should not be lenient:
biur-halacha/3:א: (טו) And the small one forbidden, etc. — for it breached in its full [length]. The rule "full" applies where the courtyard lacks a strip of four [amot] or any strip from here and there [or one tefach per one view] — called "full" — forbidden if breached to a forbidden place; if breached to a courtyard they need one eruv for both; if the breach is more than ten amot it is also a breach and forbidden [Peri Megadim]:
biur-halacha/3:ב: (יח) And when walls of the small one protrude three tefachim, etc. — not precise — for even one wall suffices [Gra]; meaning even if only one wall protrudes three tefachim and the other was less than three, still forbidden — for what they said lavud on one side requires specifically a strip from here and there or a strip four tefachim wide on one side:
biur-halacha/4:_: Breached before Shabbat in its full [length] to a large roof — the reason a small roof is not permitted in the sides of a large roof is "visible from outside and equal from inside" as above seif 3 — for regarding the large roof we say gud aciq mechitzeta and it is as if it has sides; one could say that gud aciq applies to the large roof itself but not to permit the small roof in the sides of the large [Ritva — thus the question of Derishah is resolved, brought in Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger]:
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (a) And it opened on Shabbat, etc. In responsum of Maharil siman 192 it implies forbidden when sealed intentionally unless it opened before Shabbat; and so Magen Avraham expanded to forbid.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: (b) He sealed it intentionally, etc. And even if he broke its pegs (Magen Avraham and Taz).
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: (ג) And for Rambam, etc. And the essential ruling follows the first view (Nachalat Tzvi).
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: (ד) And it was breached, etc. In its full [length] or more than ten amot — Rashi.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] They joined via window, etc. — two houses or two courtyards that joined together because there was a window or opening between them. R' Zalman Orach:
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There. And it was sealed on Shabbat — a collapse fell against it. Rashi.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (ג) There. And it was sealed on Shabbat, etc. — but if sealed while still day, even if it reopened at night they are forbidden, for they never acquired an eruv at all — acquisition of eruv is at bein hashemashot, and here there was no eruv at bein hashemashot since the opening was sealed; and from nightfall they do not acquire eruv since we do not join at nightfall; and even if they joined before the Shabbat that passed and that eruv still remains, they cannot rely on it this Shabbat after the opening opened, since it was nullified while still day and does not revive at nightfall. R' Zalman there:
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (ד) There. They are permitted to use, etc. — for Shabbat: once permitted, permitted. Gemara; Tur and Beit Yosef brought it.
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (Siman 1) And even, etc. — likewise as partners in the [eruv] bread. Meaning: even though through sealing the eruv was nullified, when it opens — even if they did not join anew — they remain partners in that bread placed initially for eruv and are partners in that bread, and need not join as above siman 366 seif 1 and below siman 386 seif 3:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: (Siman 1) If so when it opens on Shabbat, etc. — bein hashemashot did not acquire eruv, for at bein hashemashot it was still not open and the original eruv was already nullified by sealing; therefore Agur cited in Beit Yosef wrote: Maharil was asked if he sealed the opening (intentionally) and later reconsidered to open — does the eruv return to original permission for the coming Shabbat? Maharil answered: I cannot distinguish unintentional from intentional — meaning even intentional returns to original permission; and from the questioner asking if it returns for the coming Shabbat it implies that for that Shabbat — if it opened on its own on Shabbat — it is obvious to him it does not return to original permission, as Magen Avraham — since he sealed intentionally the eruv was nullified and at bein hashemashot it was still sealed, bein hashemashot did not acquire eruv; therefore Rama is difficult who permits even sealed intentionally and opened on Shabbat; certainly if sealed unintentionally it is fit to permit even if opened on Shabbat, for the eruv was never nullified; and likewise if sealed intentionally and nullified, if it opened before Shabbat bein hashemashot again acquires eruv as above — but sealed intentionally and opened this Shabbat we have not heard:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ג: (Siman 1) From ships is not proof, etc. — Rosh beginning of Eruvin siman 23: it appears that if one joined for a year from courtyard to courtyard, etc., even if sealed mid-week and opened on Shabbat the eruv returns to its place; proof from Shabbat 101 chapter HaZorek: tied ships may join and carry from one to the other; severed — forbidden; reconnected — return to original permission — for all partitions made on Shabbat, etc.; implies severed even on a weekday; for if on Shabbat, even without reconnecting we say Shabbat: once permitted, permitted — end of his words; Magen Avraham siman 355: per Tosafos there on Shabbat it is not proof — one could say ships deal with severance on Shabbat and nevertheless if not reconnected they are forbidden, and we need not say once permitted, permitted since the sea interrupts as karmelis; and such we do not say once permitted, permitted as here seif 2; and even though ships are not yet separated, since they stand to be separated they are considered separated — so Maggid Mishneh in Raavad there; see what Magen Avraham wrote to explain Rosh that he holds like Rambam:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ד: (Siman 1) Nevertheless Tosafos, etc. — meaning Rosh must disagree with Tosafos; for Tosafos there is no proof for Rosh's law; nevertheless Tosafos' own words are difficult:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ו: (Siman 1) And they brought proof from the ship — however Tosafos did not conclude as Rosh — implying severed on a weekday; for if on Shabbat we should say once permitted, permitted; rather they left their proof open: "even if sealed mid-week and afterward opened on Shabbat it is permitted, etc.; proof from chapter HaZorek: tied ships," etc., "severed — forbidden; reconnected — return to original permission" — end. And as plainly understood, their intent is as Rosh — severed on a weekday; otherwise we should say even without reconnecting, say once permitted, etc.; but then their words in Eruvin and Shabbat contradict each other:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ז: (Siman 1) Therefore we must say their proof, etc. — meaning Tosafos do not hold as Rosh; rather Tosafos hold the ship case can be explained as severed on Shabbat as in Shabbat — in any event we learn that even though forbidden, for some reason if reconnected — even if reconnected on its own without human intent — they return to original permission; likewise if severed on a weekday, if reconnected on its own on Shabbat they return to original permission; likewise opening sealed and opened even if opened on its own returns to permission:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ח: (Siman 1) However regarding intentional sealing, etc. — the baraita teaches "severed" implying on its own only; Bach wrote, etc. — see Taz siman 1:
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (Siman 2) Each one, etc. — specifically when the opening is sealed; Rambam disagrees only on the beginning of the seif:
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: (Siman 2) For even though the eruv, etc. — meaning: if we do not permit each only for itself, then why do we say once permitted for one — even though the eruv lies in another courtyard? In such a case it would be fit to forbid carrying even in the courtyard where the eruv is not placed since it cannot bring its eruv there; nevertheless since at the start of Shabbat it was possible to bring its eruv there, we say once permitted, permitted:
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: (Siman 3) To karmelis, etc. Beit Yosef wrote: permitted to carry from courtyard to karmelis, etc., for he holds since it breached to karmelis the courtyard has the law of karmelis and we hold from karmelis to karmelis carrying is permitted — within four amot; Eruvin 98:
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) And even if he sealed intentionally. For when it opens before Shabbat they are like partners in the bread, and at bein hashemashot which acquires eruv there is an opening between them fit for joining (responsum Maharil siman 192); if so when it opens on Shabbat it is forbidden, for since he sealed intentionally he revealed he does not want an eruv, and thus bein hashemashot did not acquire eruv; therefore Agur cited Maharil; and see what I wrote siman 355 seif 1 and siman 383 — Rosh's proof from ships sealed on a weekday is not proof; see there; nevertheless Tosafos 17 also wrote permitted even if opened on Shabbat and brought proof from the ship; and on 101 on Shabbat they wrote even if opened on Shabbat forbidden; therefore we must say their proof is as there automatically returns to original permission — so here; however regarding intentional sealing in the default case opening on Shabbat does not help — doubt; Bach wrote if he broke its pegs the eruv was nullified — not required; see there:
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) Each for itself. Specifically when the opening is sealed — for even though the eruv lies in another courtyard, permitted to carry for itself; but when the opening opens both return to their permission:
magen-avraham/2:_: (ב) To karmelis forbidden. Since the partitions do not stand; Beit Yosef wrote: when breached to karmelis permitted to carry from courtyard to karmelis within four amot — Eruvin 98 seif 2; and possible even though a courtyard lies upon it, forbidden to carry from it to karmelis; see Gemara 6 and 24:
magen-avraham/3:_: (ג) And the small one forbidden. For it breached in its full [length]:
magen-avraham/4:_: (ד) That the roof protrudes. Tosafos 89 implies specifically when it protrudes four per Rashi and Rashi walks under it — then that protrusion is karmelis and the entire roof is breached to it in full; see Rosh; but if it does not protrude, no — it is no worse than a pillar that is reshus ha-yachid siman 345 seif 10; nevertheless when two roofs are breached to one another they forbid one another — so Rashba Gittin 79:
mechaber/1:main: If an opening or window was sealed on Shabbat in a place where they had joined an eruv. And in it are 4 seifim: They joined via a window or opening between them and it was sealed on Shabbat — they are permitted to use via the height of the wall and its holes; and even if he joined for a year and the opening was sealed on a weekday and opened on Shabbat {Rama: and even if he sealed it intentionally (Agur)} the eruv returns to permit it; and for Rambam it is not permitted to carry except each for itself, but not from one to the other:
mechaber/2:main: There was a wall between two courtyards and each joined for itself and the wall was breached on Shabbat — they are permitted to carry, each in its courtyard, even utensils of the house; but a courtyard breached on Shabbat to reshus ha-rabbim or to karmelis is forbidden:
mechaber/3:main: A small courtyard breached before Shabbat in its full [length] to a large one and the breach is not more than ten amot — the large one is permitted to take out utensils that remained in the house to its courtyard if it joined for itself; and the small one is forbidden to take out utensils that remained in the house to its courtyard unless they joined together; and this is when the walls of the small one enter into the large one; and when the walls of the small one protrude three tefachim from the length-walls of the large one — for if not, the small one would be permitted via visible from outside and equal from inside:
mechaber/4:main: A small roof breached before Shabbat in its full [length] to a large roof — the small one is forbidden to raise onto it utensils that remained in the house; and the large one is permitted; and this is when the partitions of the house are visible to one standing on the roof; but if they are not visible — such as the roof protrudes over them — it is karmelis unless open to it from the house a window four by four:
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) And it was sealed on Shabbat — e.g. a collapse fell against it [Rashi]:
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) They are permitted to use — from one to the other on this Shabbat; and all the more so each for itself is permitted, even the one where the eruv is not placed:
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) Via the height of the wall and its holes — meaning: even though now that it is sealed they are not fit to join since the holes lack the measure of a window, nevertheless the eruv was not nullified for this Shabbat, for since it was permitted at the start of Shabbat it remains permitted for the whole Shabbat:
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) And it opened on Shabbat — meaning: not only if it opened before Shabbat is it certainly an eruv, for at entry of Shabbat they were already open to one another; rather even if it opened on Shabbat itself, since at the time of placing the eruv that he placed for many Shabbatot or a year there was an opening from one to the other and the eruv took effect — therefore even on another Shabbat when from the start of Shabbat it was sealed and then the eruv was not effective for all, nevertheless it was not nullified and as soon as it opens the eruv returns to its original permission:
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) And even if he sealed it intentionally — meaning intentionally. And know that Magen Avraham and many later authorities sided to forbid here when it reopened on Shabbat, for since he sealed the opening between the two courtyards intentionally it is like nullifying the eruv by hand — he revealed he does not want an eruv; if so, at bein hashemashot when it was still sealed it does not help when it opens later on Shabbat itself; we are not lenient when sealed intentionally except when it opened before Shabbat — then we say even if nullified initially, when it reopened they are still partners in the eruv bread and at bein hashemashot there is an opening fit for joining; see Biur Halacha where we explained practice should follow this. However if when sealing he intended only temporarily and afterward to reopen, it is reasonable to permit even when it reopened on Shabbat:
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) And for Rambam, etc. — refers to the beginning of the seif where the opening was sealed on Shabbat: per the first view permitted to use from one to the other via holes; per him not permitted except each courtyard for itself; and the stringency is that even the courtyard where the eruv is not placed is permitted; nevertheless if it reopened, all agree permitted to carry from one to the other as initially. For practice the essential ruling is like the first view, so many later authorities:
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (ז) Each in its courtyard — for though each courtyard is now breached to another domain since they are not partners, and it is breached to a place forbidden to it; nevertheless since at twilight it was permitted, it remains permitted for the whole Shabbat:
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (ח) And even utensils of the house — for courtyard utensils were permitted to carry even from courtyard to courtyard when breached, for all courtyards are one domain, as above beginning of siman 372:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (ט) But, etc. — to karmelis forbidden. Here we do not say once permitted, permitted as initially, for there it breached only to a courtyard that is private domain like it and between them is only that one belongs to this individual and one to another; but this one breached to an actual other domain — we do not say once permitted, permitted; see Biur Halacha:
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (י) That was breached before Shabbat — for if on Shabbat we say once permitted, permitted:
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (יא) In its full [length] to the large one — meaning they were adjacent and a wall separated them and this entire wall was breached:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (יב) And there is not in the breach more than ten amot — for if more than ten we cannot say the small one is like the opening of the large one — an opening more than ten amot people do not make:
mishnah-berurah/3:ד: (יג) The large one is permitted, etc. — and the small one does not forbid it, for the large one has sides and the place of the wall breach of the small one is like its opening:
mishnah-berurah/3:ה: (יד) To take out utensils that remained in the house, etc. — for utensils that remained in the courtyard are permitted l'chatchila to take out even to another courtyard even without joining together:
mishnah-berurah/3:ו: (טו) If it joined for itself — but if it did not join, it too is forbidden:
mishnah-berurah/3:ז: (טז) And the small one forbidden, etc. — for its wall breached in its full [length] to the large one which is a forbidden place for it:
mishnah-berurah/3:ח: (יז) And this is, etc. — meaning: when is the small one forbidden — when its walls enter and protrude into the large one two or three amot like this:
mishnah-berurah/3:ט: (יח) Protruding three tefachim, etc. — meaning the place where the partitions of the small one enter is protruding from the length-walls of the large one on its side; and we require three tefachim — for otherwise we say lavud to the length of the large one and it is as if not protruding at all:
mishnah-berurah/3:י: (יט) For if not so the small one would be permitted, etc. — meaning: if the walls of the small one did not enter and protrude into the large one, the small one would also be permitted, for though equal from inside — one standing inside sees all its length-walls equal with no wide wall to its sides — the breach is in its full [length]; from outside within the large one it appears to have remnants of wall on this side and that [the surplus the large has over the small would permit the small through them] — unlike when the walls of the small protrude into the large, where the remnants of the large wall behind the small breach are not relevant to it:
mishnah-berurah/4:א: (כ) Small roof, etc. — but if both roofs are equal they forbid one another even if not more than ten amot, for they breached in their full [length] to one another:
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (כא) That was breached, etc. — not precise; the intent is it was open to the adjacent roof; regarding roofs we do not deal with initially having a partition — he used the term "breached" following seif 3:
mishnah-berurah/4:ג: (כב) Before Shabbat — for if on Shabbat we say once permitted, permitted, as above:
mishnah-berurah/4:ד: (כג) In its full [length] to a large roof — meaning the entire small roof faced the adjacent large roof; also deals when they did not join their upper stories together; also the small roof does not hold more than ten amot — as above seif 3:
mishnah-berurah/4:ה: (כד) The small one forbidden to raise, etc. — for it breached to its fellow's forbidden domain:
mishnah-berurah/4:ו: (כה) That remained in the house — for utensils that remained on the roof are permitted to carry even to another's roof without any eruv, as above siman 372 seif 1:
mishnah-berurah/4:ז: (כו) And the large one permitted — to take out house utensils onto its roof, for the small roof toward it is considered like a mere opening since it is not more than ten amot:
mishnah-berurah/4:ח: (כז) Partitions of the house visible, etc. — that all their roofs were divided and not sloped; and when the roof does not protrude from the walls outward, the house partitions appear to one standing on the roof edge looking under his feet — then we say gud aciq mechitzeta and as if enclosed with partitions above around the roof; but when the roof protrudes from the walls outward the house partitions are not visible, we do not say gud aciq mechitzeta, and it is karmelis — forbidden to carry in each who lacks any partition, even utensils that remained on the roof, except within four amot:
mishnah-berurah/4:ט: (כח) That the roof protrudes — specifically when it protrudes four tefachim; but if it does not protrude four tefachim it is like visible partitions [Magen Avraham and Eliyah Rabbah; see what we wrote above siman 345 seif 16 in Biur Halacha]:
mishnah-berurah/4:י: (כט) Open to it, etc. — for they use it and the entire roof is considered holes of reshus ha-yachid; nevertheless this helps only to permit use on his roof with utensils that remained inside which thereby has reshus ha-yachid name on it; but to raise onto it utensils that remained in the house is forbidden in any case when they did not join together, since the partitions are not visible on it:
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham siman 1) If so when it opens on Shabbat — forbidden. Note: and to reconcile — Rama's intent is also when he opened before Shabbat, and he teaches us like when sealed on its own and opened on its own on a weekday — likewise if sealing and opening were intentional it is permitted; know that if we explained Rama's words as when it opens on Shabbat, his gloss should precede "opened on Shabbat"; but Levush wrote: sealed intentionally — even if opened on Shabbat — no distinction:
netiv-chayim/2:_: (Magen Avraham siman 5) In Tosafos it implies. Note: truly they initially explain thus; but afterward Tosafos conclude Yerushalmi does not hold thus — a roof protruding four tefachim, since it lacks partitions, is a makom patur; and they explain all these passages per Yerushalmi — thus even with less than four protrusion it is makom patur; but Rosh, Tur, and Shulchan Aruch ruled like Rashi's view — for them our roofs are karmelis even without four protrusion:
netiv-chayim/3:_: (Magen Avraham siman 5) And so in the Gemara. Note: he does not know from where he took it; if because it asks: let us learn two gezuztraot for Shmuel and does not ask Rav — perhaps because we could say Rav is not asked here either, for until here Rav disagrees only regarding this via lowering and that via throwing; but with two forces — this via lowering and throwing and that via lowering — Rav agrees both are not forbidden. And if you say: if Rav were asked too, what does Rav Ada bar Ahavah answer — then Rav's dispute between adjacent and protruding would be difficult — why is protruding different with four, behold there is a ladder beneath from lower to upper. And one could say Rav Ada truly answers only for Shmuel, and Abaye comes to resolve both Rav and Shmuel; and if he means the Talmud's answer on 85 — perhaps here it is different since this is via throwing air and that via lowering, implying only throwing air; but in adjacency which is via lowering and throwing height both are forbidden — one could say this variant establishes the mishnah like Abaye, e.g. standing within ten as Maharsha wrote; see there:
peri-megadim/1:א: (א) And even — in siman 372 Bach implies he holds: even though sealed on a weekday intentionally and opened on Shabbat it is permitted; and on this he wrote: if he broke its pegs on a weekday and opened on Shabbat — forbidden; and so Rabbenu Yerucham in gloss — even if sealed intentionally by a gentile and opened on Shabbat by gentile or Jew the eruv returns to its place; and Magen Avraham letter 1; and Taz holds: even if he broke pegs, whenever it opens on Shabbat the eruv returns to original permission; proof: Rosh and Tosafos Eruvin 17 s.v. "eruv" wrote: sealed on a weekday and opened on Shabbat returns to permission; or it fell on its own and was sealed — nevertheless he diverted attention not to open on Shabbat, yet permitted because it opened on Shabbat; and proof from ships Tosafos and Rosh brought — tied and permitted and reconnected return to permission — meaning permitted at twilight; for if on Shabbat once permitted, permitted; if so certainly he diverted attention and it is permitted — likewise intentional and breaking pegs, whenever it opens on Shabbat returns to first permission; Bach could say: with direct action it does not:
peri-megadim/1:ב: And know what is written "joined for a year" — it is an inference; or they joined at twilight and it was fit that the eruv acquire — there was an opening and it was sealed afterward at twilight and opened on Shabbat; even though at Shabbat start in eruv matters it was not permitted, the eruv took effect when it opened; strained to say specifically for a year since perhaps he minimized the eruv — doubt; and what Taz wrote "and they were permitted on Shabbat" — perhaps they were permitted — severed at twilight; and the word "on Shabbat" refers afterward: he diverted attention not to reconnect on Shabbat. The rule here: when Shabbat enters it was permitted even if sealed afterward it was permitted; conversely also forbidden at Shabbat start and repaired on Shabbat — since at making the eruv it was fit and sealed and opened afterward on Shabbat — permitted. If part of twilight the opening was open and within twilight it was sealed — one could say it was not permitted; certainly though if eaten at twilight the eruv acquires well siman 392 and 394; nevertheless once permitted we say only in a clear matter — doubt; and with God's help more in Magen Avraham:
peri-megadim/2:_: (ב) They are permitted — in siman 372: all that have partitions and one domain only belonging to two individuals — we say once permitted, permitted; not so breached to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelis. Eruvin 98 and what Magen Avraham wrote:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Magen Avraham siman 3 page siman 372 seif 2. In my humble opinion it is explicit in Tosafos Shabbat 9a in what they wrote "or," etc. — e.g. open to karmelis and larger than it — we find Eruvin 90: requires two amot; and one authority in a portico — how? Rashi there: in a portico more than two se'ah which is karmelis — in my portico certainly permitted, for no change in ownership; rather required in another's portico — though also reshus ha-yachid, nevertheless since forbidden to carry four amot because breached to a place forbidden to it — to another roof permitted to carry from it to karmelis; one can reject: only in a portico which is also full reshus ha-yachid and throwing into it one is liable — only because more than se'ah they forbade carrying; therefore comparable to this roof; but to another karmelis one could say forbidden to carry since the roof is full reshus ha-yachid; however in Tosafos there and in Perush Rabbeinu Tam: "they asked — required on roof and on pillar" — meaning a pillar nine high which is karmelis — they said on it: karmelis and reshus ha-yachid are required — meaning the roof is considered reshus ha-yachid in height because eruv of houses permits carrying in all of it — implying without that reason it would be permitted to carry from this roof to karmelis; likewise a courtyard breached to karmelis as I wrote:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Seif 4: in its full [length] to a large roof forbidden to raise. For when we say gud aciq regarding the large roof itself, not to permit the small roof in the sides of the large. So Ritva. And in Derishah one authority wrote — see there:
turei-zahav/1:_: And even if he sealed intentionally. Mahariv z"l wrote; and it appears to me to distinguish: if he broke its pegs the eruv was nullified; if he did not break its pegs — when he sealed his opening he did not remove his mezuzah, lintel, and threshold — he revealed he did not remove it for himself; the eruv returns to its place; thus the Talmud distinguishes Bava Batra chapter 1 daf 11 — end; but here we are not concerned with diverting attention, for if so when it fell on a weekday and was not repaired before Shabbat he certainly diverted attention at Shabbat entry; and likewise ships that were tied and permitted on Shabbat — certainly he diverted attention they would not be repaired on Shabbat — this only when the essence depends on the eruv act: since it was fit at that hour, even if later ruined, when repaired later we are not concerned; and the eruv returns to its place:
turei-zahav/2:_: They are permitted to carry. Since it did not breach to another domain but to a courtyard — unlike the latter case where it breached to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelis:
yad-ephraim/1:_: There in Magen Avraham siman 5: but if it does not protrude four — not as written; meaning: if it protrudes four, which is an important place in its own right, the entire roof is as breached to karmelis; but if the protrusion is not four, since the roof itself is reshus ha-yachid — we say gud aciq from its six sides like a pillar — therefore Rashi 89 on visible partitions: all agree we say gud aciq on them like a pillar in Rosh Hashana which is reshus ha-yachid due to gud aciq; and since the roof itself with three partitions is reshus ha-yachid, the protrusion too is considered reshus ha-yachid — since it lacks four to be important in itself it is nullified to reshus ha-yachid and is like holes of reshus ha-yachid; and one could say: since here are only three partitions for the roof itself, forbidden to carry until repair in the fourth as explained siman 363 letter 7 — specifically when breached in the fourth to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelis — unlike here where the public does not control the roof as Tosafos there; also there is no karmelis since it is not four wide — makom patur; and breaching to makom patur does not forbid carrying; therefore Tosafos wrote: if the protrusion is four the whole roof is forbidden as breached in full to karmelis; but because the roof has only three partitions no repair needed unless breached to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelis — therefore when protrusion is not four, carrying on the whole roof is fine, also on the protrusion since considered reshus ha-yachid nullified to it or like holes of reshus ha-yachid even if not four wide; see 87b: they are like holes of karmelis — here beginning as karmelis the amah entering the city though lacking karmelis measure is called holes of karmelis; likewise here considered holes of reshus ha-yachid; see siman 321 siman 5 and what is written there:
